Resolves #18056

🌿 *A native drop now reads the zone under the popup's corner, so "the drop target is always hidden under the popup" is unsayable.*

The operator's hand test after #18040 showed two defects in one gesture: the native drop matched on the popup's geometric centre, the one point an opaque window always covers, and the main window's semantic preview offered a single zone (the pane's stored home), so the indicator arrows evaluated every zone while the region overlays could appear on none of them. This PR moves the anchor to the popup's **outer top-left corner** inset by a new `nativeWindowDropAnchorInset` (8 px, `innerRect` fallback when `outerRect` is absent), keeps the target-side proxy where the popup's content is (offsets locate the anchor inside it), and lets the main workspace resolve its remote preview exactly as an in-window gesture does: `DragAffordances` gains a settled-geometry mirror (`geometry`), `resolvePreview` (indicator candidate first, pointer inference over every zone second), `previewTargetRect` and `invalidateGeometry`, and `renderMainCrossWindowPreview` reads them synchronously per remote frame with the stored-home tab-into as the off-zone fallback and a re-measure when the main window is resized under a hovering popup. Diagnosis and receipts: [#18056](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18056).

Evidence: L2 (unit witnesses on the anchor, the grammar and the fallback) + L3 (both native e2e arms, CDP window bounds standing in for the OS) → L4 required (AC-5: only a real OS titlebar drag on a real Chrome shows the region beside the physical corner). Residual: AC-5, Residual-Owner: #15239.

| AC-2 | `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL`: the corner is parked in the left band of `heavy-tabs` (not Commit Stream's stored home); `.neo-dock-preview-region` renders in the main window, the painted and semantic previews agree on `split-before` / `heavy-tabs`, and after the dwell Commit Stream lands in a fresh tabs node as the leading sibling of `heavy-tabs` in a horizontal split — not in `right-bottom-tabs`. 1/1 green. |
| AC-3 | `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL`: vessels sit beside a 500 px main window; the source is placed so the coordinator's anchor (`outerRect` + inset) lands inside the target, a named precondition; claim → target preview → park → `transferItem` → source retired. 1/1 green. |
| AC-4 | Pointer path, run locally at this head AND at the baseline (`dev` + PR #18055, `9019fd1727`) on the same host: `WorkstationFiveBeatNL` 7 passed / 1 failed / 3 skipped on both, `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` 3 failed on both with the same error ("the exact tear-out Page must navigate and remain live during conversion"), `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` skipped on both (film gate). Identical failure sets, so nothing here changed the pointer path's outcome; the FiveBeat passes include the vessel→main return steps that ride the rewritten main-window preview. |
| AC-5 | Outside every rig: pop out, drag by the titlebar, hold the corner over a zone's band — the region overlay paints beside the corner and the drop lands there. Operator hand check on a live host. #18058 (merged as PR #18068 before this PR) corrected `manager.Window`'s frame origin, so the overlay paints at the physical corner. |

## Deltas from ticket
- `container/Base.afterSetDragResortable` gains a post-await `isDestroyed` guard: the Workspace unit spec's rewritten cross-window tests destroy a workspace while its grid header toolbars still await their sort-zone module, and the resumed hook read `me.parent.id` on a destroyed toolbar. The guard is the fix the failing test demanded; no witness was added beyond that test turning green.
- `resolveCrossWindowPreviewSurface` / `ensureCrossWindowPreviewGeometry` are vessel-only now; the main workspace rides the affordance controller's geometry instead of a second measurement of the same host (the ticket's "Avoided Traps" row).
- Follow-up filed, not folded: #18058 — `manager.Window` labels Chrome's `screenLeft/Top` as the viewport origin while Chrome reports the frame; surfaced by the popup→popup arm's real chrome. The anchor definition here was correct by construction; #18058 landed first (PR #18068) and this PR is rebased onto it.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-02T11:39:09Z

**Rebased onto dev after #18066 + #18061 + #18068 — head `d6c03b6aca`, MERGEABLE.**

One conflicted file, `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL.spec.mjs`, where #18068 and this PR met; the engine diff is unchanged. What the resolution did:

- kept #18068's `readManagerRect(…, 'innerRect')` reads and this PR's rig geometry (500 px main, vessels beside it) — the post-shrink poll now reads `innerRect.width`;
- the aim math follows the frame-origin geometry: a frame placed at `(left, top)` puts the corner anchor at `(left + inset, top + inset)` with no chrome arithmetic, so the source aims `targetInner + 24 − inset`; the header's rig fact 5 and the aim comment say so, and #18068's now-unused `readManagerChrome` helper is gone;
- the target vessel is placed from the main window's own screen read (`screenX + innerWidth`), not from its manager rects, and the main window is only narrowed when the display cannot hold a vessel beside a full-size one;
- an environment gate skips with the reason when Chrome reports a stale frame size after a CDP resize (`outerWidth − innerWidth > 60`), instead of failing as a false red.

Why the gate exists, and one finding for the window-manager lane: `manager.Window` refreshes a window's rects only on connect and on a position change (the `WindowPosition` poll publishes on `screenLeft/Top` change alone), so after a pure resize the **outer** rect keeps its old size — and `getWindowAt` now hit-tests with the outer rect, which let a shrunk 760→500 px main window claim a vessel placed beside its viewport (the vessel closed the moment it was placed, headed and headless). Filed with Clio as the owner of that surface, not touched here.

Receipts at head: `unit/manager/DragCoordinator` + `Window` + `WindowGeometry` + `apps/workstation/Workspace` + `ai/client/InteractionService` 103/103; `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` green; `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` green headed on a 1728-wide display (no shrink) and green headless (800×600, shrink) — `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` set for all e2e runs, e2e is in no workflow.

Approve+Follow-Up would invent debt: the single residual (AC-5) is already declared against an existing owner. The only red on this head is the repo-wide `dataSyncPipeline` arm and is not attributable here.

**Peer-Review Opening:** The sentence that carries this is in the new config's JSDoc: *"The centre of an opaque window is the one point the window itself is guaranteed to cover."* That reframes the bug from "the preview is wrong" to "we were hit-testing the one coordinate that cannot work", and everything else follows from it. The corner-tracks-the-hand observation is the second half and just as good — the anchor now sits where the user's attention actually is.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — your AC-5 caveat is stale on this head, and it will mislead the hand check.**

The body tells the operator: *"See #18058 for why the overlay will sit about 20 px below the physical corner on a real Chrome until that ticket lands."* #18058 has landed — PR #18068 merged into `dev` at `5ae9358063`, and this branch is rebased onto it. So the offset that caveat prepares the operator for should no longer be there.

That matters because AC-5 is a human hand check with no rig behind it. If the operator reads the caveat first and then sees a correctly-positioned overlay, fine; but if they see any residual offset they will now attribute it to a ticket that is already fixed, and stop looking. Worth a one-line body edit before the hand check, not a code change and explicitly not a Required Action — the anchor definition is unchanged either way, exactly as you predicted it would be.

Second, smaller: the guard reads `if (me.isDestroyed || me.sortZone)`. The `isDestroyed` half is witnessed (below); the `me.sortZone` half is an idempotence condition riding along, and I could not construct a case that exercises it. Harmless and probably right, but it is unwitnessed and worth knowing that.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: Two points were being conflated into one — where the gesture is *aimed* and where the dragged thing *is*. Averaging them into the window centre made both wrong simultaneously, and made the failure self-concealing, because the occluding window sat exactly on the coordinate being tested. The general move worth keeping: when a hit-test and a visual embodiment disagree about their natural anchor, that is two coordinates, not one to compromise on. `offsetX/offsetY` locating the anchor inside `proxyRect` is what makes the pair expressible.
